query: Which material can be used for enhanced catalytic activity and durability toward HER and HOR, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A compositionally tuned high-entropy alloy catalyst, engineered via high‐throughput alloy synthesis, will exhibit enhanced catalytic activity and durability for both the hydrogen evolution (HER) and hydrogen oxidation (HOR) reactions in acidic media compared to standard catalysts.
generation.material_initial_state: A disordered, near-equiatomic multi-component (high-entropy) alloy in a solid solution state.
generation.intervention: Systematic composition adjustments leveraging high‐throughput synthesis to identify the optimal ratios of catalytically active elements (e.g., transition metals such as Ni, Co, Mo, etc.)
generation.conditions: Acidic electrolyte (0.5 M H2SO4) under standard HER/HOR operational conditions along with accelerated durability testing using rotating disk electrode (RDE) characterization.
generation.structural_mediator: A homogeneous disordered structure that provides a synergistic distribution of active sites and electronic modifications between neighboring atoms.
generation.mechanism: Multiple principal elements within the high-entropy alloy create a synergistic effect where the electronic structure of the active sites is optimally tuned for hydrogen adsorption/desorption, reducing overpotentials while also enhancing resistance to corrosion and dissolution under acidic conditions.
generation.predicted_outcome: The optimized high-entropy alloy catalyst will demonstrate lower overpotentials, higher exchange current densities for both HER and HOR, and improved durability compared to conventional Pt-based or unoptimized alloy catalysts under the same testing conditions.
generation.baseline: Standard catalysts, such as typical Pt-based catalysts or conventional alloy catalysts tested under identical conditions.
generation.boundary: The improvements are expected only within a compositional window where the alloy remains a single-phase disordered solid solution; compositions that lead to phase separation or intermetallic compound formation may not yield the enhanced performance.
generation.uncertainty: The precise elemental ratios and the magnitude of the performance enhancement are not known a priori and require further optimization and mechanistic investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of high-entropy alloy catalysts with systematically varied compositions using high‐throughput methods. Characterize their HER and HOR performance in 0.5 M H2SO4 using rotating disk electrode (RDE) techniques under both standard operational conditions and accelerated durability tests.
measurements: Overpotential at a fixed current density
Durability metrics (e.g., current retention over time, stability under accelerated degradation protocols)
Structural and compositional analysis to verify the single-phase solid solution state
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If none of the tested alloy compositions show statistically significant improvements in both catalytic activity (lower overpotential and higher exchange current densities) and durability compared to the baseline standard catalysts, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: High entropy alloys (HEAs), complex concentrated alloys (CCAs), and multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) are the most common names of a new group of materials [ [1] , [2] , [3] , [4] , [5] ] introduced by Yeh et al. [ [6] ] and Cantor et al. [ [7] ] in the beginning of this century. Many definitions were proposed for such materials, but in general they consist of multiple (usually at least five) elements in equiatomic or near-equiatomic composition [ [2] ]. This approach is different from the traditional alloy design using one (or maximum two) principal element and other minor elements. The presence of many elements in equiatomic (or near) composition leads to high mixing entropy and thus to many interesting properties [ [2] , [5] ]. One of such effects is the existence of a random solid solution and simple body centered cubic (bcc) or faced centered cubic (fcc) structure. Recently HEAs with hexagonal closed packed (hcp) structure have been reported as well [ [8] , [9] ]. A new approach to HEA design using the valence electron concentration (VEC) was recently proposed with the aim of increasing the plasticity of these alloys [ [10] , [11] ].
